analysis: What changed vs the 6 AM brief: the green futures tape survived the open but fragmented immediately. The 6 AM story was a broad AI-supply-chain bid (Celestica/Cadence) with banks as the offset; the 7 AM tape is narrower — Celestica is still the standout and Tesla is still running on its own upgrade, but Meta, Microsoft and Apple all opened lower, so the rally is not broadening. Earnings grading is strict this morning: UPS's beat-and-raise is the only clean reward, Coca-Cola's beat-and-raise slipped, and Boeing's revenue beat was overridden by an EPS miss. That pattern — guidance lifts not automatically lifting stocks — is the signal to carry into Wednesday's Microsoft/Alphabet prints. Signal: Celestica holding a double-digit gain, the megacap split, UPS vs KO/BA divergence, the 10 a.m. ET confidence print. Noise: the premarket micro-cap gainers, the SK Hynix special-dividend report (still single-source, unconfirmed), and Anthropic IPO valuation chatter (no confirmed price range). The open inherits a green but selective tape, with the 10 a.m. ET data as the next macro input before Wednesday's Fed decision.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: The open kept the green futures tape but turned stock-specific fast: in the first ~30 minutes, Tesla (+2.9%), Nvidia (+0.24%), Alphabet (+0.21%) and Amazon (+0.03%) were higher, while Meta (-1.20%), Microsoft (-0.65%) and Apple (-0.30%) were lower, per Finnhub early-session snapshots.
headlines.why_it_matters: No broad risk-on/risk-off read in the first half hour — earnings and deal headlines, not the index, are deciding the tape.

headlines.headline: Celestica held a double-digit gain into the open, up 11.7% to $275.59 (open $264.31, prior close $246.65) after Q3 revenue jumped 83% to $5.83B and adjusted EPS of $3.30 beat estimates; its $40B 2027 revenue guide is well above the $35.5B consensus, though the gain cooled from the 15-17% premarket range.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI-hardware demand print is holding, not just gapping and fading — the supply-chain leg of the AI trade has real support into the hyperscaler prints.

headlines.headline: Tesla rose 2.9% to $402.97 in early trading (prior close $391.62), adding to Monday's 5.21% jump after Barclays upgraded it to overweight, citing a possible SpaceX combination and stronger core operations.
headlines.why_it_matters: Second straight day of upgrade-driven strength — Tesla is still running on its own catalyst rather than the AI tape.

headlines.headline: Meta fell 1.20% to $623.02 in early trading (prior close $630.56) after pricing its upsized $25B common offering at $625 a share, with Nvidia confirmed as a $3B participant and Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom indicating non-binding interest in up to $5B combined; Nvidia itself was up just 0.24% to $216.52.
headlines.why_it_matters: Dilution is outweighing deal enthusiasm in the first half hour — the offering is priced in, and Meta now needs earnings, not headlines, to stabilize.

headlines.headline: Coca-Cola beat and raised but slipped: Q3 comparable EPS of $0.91 topped the $0.88 consensus and full-year comparable EPS growth guidance was raised to at least 11% (from 9-10%), yet shares were down 0.49% to $92.25 in early trading (prior close $92.70).
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat-and-raise that does not lift the stock in the first half hour — expectations were already high after a strong run into the print.

headlines.headline: UPS rose 1.74% to $102.07 in early trading (prior close $100.32) after Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.69 beat the $1.62-1.63 consensus and revenue of $22.9B beat estimates; it raised full-year revenue guidance to ~$92.6B and adjusted EPS guidance to $7.28 (from $7.22).
headlines.why_it_matters: A clean beat-and-raise into the holiday shipping season — the one large-cap morning print that is being rewarded straightforwardly.

headlines.headline: Boeing fell 1.31% to $185.85 in early trading (prior close $188.31) after its Q3 loss narrowed to $116M from $5.34B a year ago on revenue up ~4% to $24.19B, but EPS of -$0.34 missed the -$0.25 consensus.
headlines.why_it_matters: Turnaround progress is real but the EPS miss is what the tape is trading — revenue beat alone is not enough this morning.

headlines.headline: PayPal slipped close to 1% premarket despite lifting its annual adjusted profit view, then steadied to +0.25% at $55.13 in early trading (prior close $54.99) — a mixed reaction rather than a clean earnings move.
headlines.why_it_matters: Guidance lifts are being graded harshly this morning — PayPal shows a raised outlook can still open soft if the print itself does not excite.

headlines.headline: Carried forward: HSBC was down about 6.9% premarket after Q3 pretax profit of $9.63B missed expectations despite a new $1B buyback; it remains the morning's bank-sector drag.
headlines.why_it_matters: Banks are still the tape's offset — a big-bank miss keeps any rally narrow if the open's leaders fade.

headlines.headline: Carried forward: Apple is to replace iPhone Duo units affected by the inner-display cracking issue reported after its Oct 23 launch, and Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees two days before its fiscal Q1 print Wednesday after the close; in early trading Apple was down 0.30% to $342.90 and Microsoft down 0.65% to $529.12.
headlines.why_it_matters: Both names enter their earnings window with live overhangs — Duo replacements for Apple, buyout framing for Microsoft — and both opened soft.

headlines.headline: Macro carried forward: September durable goods rose 1.8% (headline beat) but core orders rose only 0.5% (slight miss); the Fed's two-day meeting begins today with the decision due Wednesday 2:00 p.m. ET and a hold widely expected.
headlines.why_it_matters: No macro reset this morning — the split durable-goods print and a priced-in Fed hold leave the tape to earnings until the 10 a.m. ET data.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news this morning. The Q3 distribution of $0.525 per common unit ($2.10 annualized, ~8.4% yield) went ex-dividend Monday Oct 26 and pays Nov 6. Q3 earnings arrive before the open Tue Nov 3 with an 11 a.m. ET call. Last reported quarter (Q2, Aug 4): EPS $0.31 beat the $0.28 consensus, revenue $342.15M vs $340.49M expected. Background: on Oct 1 the partnership issued 34.5M non-convertible Class A units at a fixed 9.25% annual distribution rate in an internal reorganization, and it now trades on the Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE) after moving from NYSE on Oct 5. WTI easing to $101.05 keeps crude near six-week highs, so the energy backdrop for compression demand stays supportive with no company-specific catalyst.
